Origin: Afar Triangle (Ethiopia), site of many important fossil finds.
Boxgrove, village in England and site of discovery of Homo heidelbergensis fossils and direct evidence of hunting and butchering by early humans.
Cashel, town in County Laois, Ireland, near which the preserved body of a young adult male, Cashel Man, was found in a bog; one of the oldest known “bog bodies” in Europe and dates to ~2000 BCE.
Hadar (Ethiopia), the paleontological fossil site within the Afar Triangle where the Lucy fossil was discovered in 1974.
Kennewick, city in Washington state, USA, near which Kennewick Man, a 9,300 BP human male skeleton discovered in 1996.
Luzia Woman, a 11,500 year-old female skeleton found at Lapa Vermelha in Brazil; named as an homage to the Lucy fossil.
Minatogawa limestone quarry (Okinawa, Japan) where four skeletons of early Homo sapiens (20,000-22,000 BCE) were excavated in 1968, 1970, and 1974.
Lake Mungo (New South Wales, Australia) is the site of three significant finds of human including Mungo woman, one of the earliest known cremations.
Narmada River Valley (India), site of Narmada Human, fossil remains of an indeterminate hominin species, the oldest found in India (50,000 – 150,000 BCE).
Natunuku, village and archeological site Natunuku VL1/1 on Viti Levu Island (Fiji), where the earliest known human skeleton from the Lapita culture was excavated.
Olduvai Gorge (Tanzania), a major paleoanthropological site.
Windover Pond, a site in Florida, USA, yielding remains of 168 individuals (including soft tissue) dating from ~7300 years BP.
